genesis.35.p1.b1.text: Arise, go up to Bethel, and settle there. Build an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you fled from your brother Esau.

genesis.35.p1.b2.text: Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you. Purify yourselves and change your garments.

genesis.35.p1.b3.text: So they gave Jacob all their foreign gods and all their earrings, …

genesis.35.p1.b4.text: … and Jacob buried them under the oak near Shechem.

genesis.35.p2.b1.text: As they set out, a terror from God fell over the surrounding cities, so that they did not pursue Jacob’s sons.

genesis.35.p2.b2.text: So Jacob and everyone with him arrived in Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan.

genesis.35.p2.b3.text: There Jacob built an altar, and he called that place El-bethel, because it was there that God had revealed Himself to Jacob as he fled from his brother.

genesis.35.p2.b4.text: Now Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died and was buried under the oak below Bethel. So Jacob named it Allon-bachuth.

genesis.35.p3.b1.text: After Jacob had returned from Paddan-aram, God appeared to him again and blessed him.

genesis.35.p3.b2.text: Though your name is Jacob, you will no longer be called Jacob. Instead, your name will be Israel.

genesis.35.p3.b3.text: I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation—even a company of nations—shall come from you, and kings shall descend from you.

genesis.35.p3.b4.text: So Jacob set up a pillar in the place where God had spoken with him—a stone marker—and he poured out a drink offering on it and anointed it with oil.

genesis.35.p4.b1.text: Later, they set out from Bethel, and while they were still some distance from Ephrath, Rachel began to give birth, and her labor was difficult.

genesis.35.p4.b2.text: Do not be afraid, for you are having another son.

genesis.35.p4.b3.text: And with her last breath—for she was dying—she named him Ben-oni. …

genesis.35.p5.b1.text: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

genesis.35.p5.b2.text: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave; it marks Rachel’s tomb to this day.

genesis.35.p5.b3.text: Israel again set out and pitched his tent beyond the Tower of Eder.

genesis.35.p6.b1.text: While Israel was living in that region, … Israel heard about it.

genesis.35.p6.b3.text: The sons of Rachel were Joseph and Benjamin.

genesis.35.p7.b1.text: Jacob returned to his father Isaac at Mamre, near Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac had stayed.

genesis.35.p7.b2.text: And Isaac lived 180 years. Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years. …

genesis.35.p7.b3.text: And his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.
